description.p: Foldav is a file manager for the files in your Nextcloud: folders are copied, moved and deleted on the server in one request, not file by file.

ul.li: Connects through GNOME Online Accounts or a browser sign-in, to more than one account
Packages of each release: a Flatpak, a tarball, a .deb, Fedora RPMs on COPR and the AUR packages foldav, foldav-git and foldav-bin; a new app icon

Folders open at once: what was listed of each is kept on this device and shown first, then the server is asked in the background; by the folder's ETag, so a folder that did not change costs one small request, not a listing of everything in it. The tree and the columns fill from it too, also after a restart

A window as Nautilus': the files as icons, a list (sorted by clicking a column's header) or columns, one per folder from the root, switched in the header or with Ctrl+1 to 3; back and forward (Alt+Left, Alt+Right) and the folder above (Alt+Up); a path bar with a segment for each folder; Show Hidden Files (Ctrl+H)

The columns view as the Files extension "My Computer" has it: rows as there, the selection in the column you work in in the accent colour and the way to it grey; a preview column for a file (its icon, name, type, size and date); the columns resized by dragging their edge, and the width kept; Left and Right between columns; a click on a column's empty room closes the columns after it

Favorites, as in Nextcloud Files: a star on files and folders (Add to Favorites in the right-click menu, the path bar's menu for the folder shown, Ctrl+D), the favorite folders listed in the sidebar (right click removes one). They are the server's, so they show on all your devices and in the web app, kept here and sent when the server can be reached; what is starred elsewhere shows when the window comes to the front or on a reload
A sidebar with the accounts (only with more than one; changing the account keeps the folder shown where the new one has it), the favorite folders of the account and a tree of its folders

New folder (Ctrl+Shift+N), rename (F2), cut, copy and paste (a copy of a name taken is named "a (copy)"), and delete to the trash bin, each one request to the server whatever the size of the folder, from the keys, the header or a right click; several files selected at once; Ctrl+Z, or Undo on the toast, takes back a rename, move or deletion

The first version of the Linux app: sign in with GNOME Online Accounts, the browser or a login name and app password, with more than one account; the folders and files of each account's Nextcloud Files, opened by a click, with Alt+Up to the parent folder; Preferences (style, accounts, settings synced between devices); a Polish translation
